articles.title: Keralam CM Satheesan says he too is victim of online attacks, alleges ‘important individual’ behind fake news campaign
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said that he himself was a victim of online attacks, and that an “important individual” was behind the dissemination of such fake news.
At a post-Cabinet press briefing, Mr. Satheesan was responding to questions on the online attacks on Congress party leaders and members of the late former Chief Minister Oommen Chandy’s family.

Mr. Satheesan also displayed copies of social media cards with his photograph which purportedly claim that the government had decided to discontinue the welfare pensions and another attributed to Chandy Oommen that Mr. Satheesan was among the individuals who had caused anguish to his father and Oommen Chandy. “Many such fake news were are being spread in the name of mainstream media organisations,” he said.
“All this comes from one centre, led by an important individual,” he said, but declined to name the person.

On the internal conflicts within the Congress involving MPs Rajmohan Unnithan and Shafi Parambil, Mr. Satheesan said he did not wish to comment on “organisational matters.” Such questions should be posed to KPCC president Sunny Joseph, he said.
Mr. Satheesan said the discussions regarding appointments to the top posts of boards and corporations under the State government were in the final stages.

Mr. Satheesan’s response came amid criticism from within the Congress party and UDF constituents such as the Revolutionary Socialist Party (RSP) that the appointments were not finalised even after the UDF government had completed six months in power.
Mr. Satheesan said the appointments would be made soon and the talks were in the final stages.

On Monday, after a State secretariat meeting of the RSP, its leader N.K. Premachandran had sharply criticised the delay and also the “absence” of regular meetings of the UDF. The RSP also wanted the appointments to be completed, if possible, this month itself.
On his part, Mr. Satheesan sought to play down the RSP leader’s remarks, saying that it was not criticism as such, and that the party merely wanted the board, corporation division completed quickly.

articles.title: 30 missing terrorists from Reasi exfiltrated to Pakistan for arms training, disturb peace in India: DGP
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Thirty terrorists hailing from Reasi district, who had gone missing between 1991 and 2003, have exfiltrated to Pakistan and are working for a terror outfit, supplying arms, ammunition and money to revive terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir, Director General of Police Nalin Prabhat said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).

The police chief said Mahore Police Station received information through reliable sources that 30 terrorists hailing from Mahore and Chassana, missing since 1991 to 2003, had crossed over to Pakistan for weapons training for waging war against India.

"These persons are now working for HM [Hizbul Mujahideen] in Pakistan and are supplying arms and ammunition, money, to promote terrorism in J&K, besides instigating and radicalising the youth for taking part in terror activities in the area," the DGP said on X.

The 30 terrorists operating from Pakistan have been identified as Mohd Qayoom of Shadole, Mohd Sabdar of Shajroo, Ghulam Mohd and Ghulam Qadir, both sons of Samdoo and residents of Khour, Mushtaq Ahmad of Khour and Khushal Hussain, a resident of Dada.

articles.title: Air passenger services see 35% inflation in Q2; banking, securities transaction witness deflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Air passenger services recorded 35.52% inflation in the July-September quarter, recording the highest rate of price rise among the seven major services for which the inflation data was released on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).

Securities transaction services and banking services, however, recorded a deflation of 6.93% and 3.96% respectively, the provisional Service Producer Price Indices (PPI) for the second quarter of 2026-27 released by the Commerce and Industry Ministry showed.
The PPI has inflation data for seven major services — Banking, Securities Transaction, Insurance, Management of Pension Funds, Railways, Air (Passenger), and Telecom — with base year 2022-23.
Service PPI measures the change in the average prices received by producers on production of a service.
As per the data, inflation in Air (Passenger) Services rose 35.52% YoY in the second quarter, compared to 31.94% in the first quarter.
Annual inflation in the railway passenger service price index rose 2.17% during the September quarter, lower than 3.50% in the June quarter.
Inflation in 'Banking Service Contribution' was 3.86% in Q2 of FY27, higher than 2.62% in Q1. The 'Banking Service Price' witnessed 3.96% deflation in Q2, vis-a-vis 4.98% deflation in Q1.
Securities Transaction Service Prices saw a deflation of 6.93% in Q2, compared to 1.32% deflation in June quarter.

Pension fund management, insurance and telecom services recorded an inflation of 1.01%, 0.49% and 0.54%, respectively in September quarter, compared to 5.48%, 0.98% and 0.72%, respectively in the June quarter.
The government would eventually include more services in the Service PPI data.

The government in June came out with the maiden PPI data for both goods and services to better reflect price movement at producer's level, paving the way for phasing out wholesale price index (WPI)-based inflation numbers in the next five years. Thereafter, in August the services PPI data was issued.

articles.title: Global climate talks must shut door on fossil fuel ‘clout’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The failure of the United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, to agree on its central political statement, with countries unable to bridge their differences over fossil fuels and other key questions of climate action, has exposed the fragility of international climate cooperation. It should also sharpen scrutiny of who gets access to climate negotiations, whose interests they represent and what safeguards keep decisions accountable to the public.

The Türkiye summit ended without agreement on an overarching statement. UN climate chief Simon Stiell said he shared the “deep disappointment” of many that the conference was unable to reach consensus on a statement that typically sends a policy signal to all nations. Some separate negotiating decisions were reached though. Nevertheless, the absence of a political consensus was a serious setback.

The breakdown does not show that fossil fuel lobbying caused the impasse. But it does make more urgent a separate question about the credibility of the process. A forum that asks governments to make decisions in the global public interest must be transparent about who is seeking to shape those decisions, what interests they represent and how conflicts are managed.

The international climate negotiations that take place every year still lack a comprehensive, enforceable system to identify and manage conflicts of interest involving powerful commercial interests, including fossil fuel companies and state-owned energy businesses. The Antalya conference has underlined why that gap matters.

articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.
Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return.
Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling.

“Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation.
“Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.”
The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23).
The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025.
Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.
The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

Neocloud and data-center companies, which came under sharp selling pressure earlier following Mr. Huang’s abrupt exit, also climbed. CoreWeave rose 21.5%, IREN gained 26.4% and Nebius advanced ⁠23.4%.
The S&P 500 information technology sector jumped 8.9% and led the gains in the benchmark index.

articles.title: Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 years as recent measures take effect, Petroleum Ministry says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The government expects domestic oil and gas production to pick up in the next 4-5 years as several steps taken in the recent past begin to bear fruit in an industry typically characterised by long gestation periods, The Hindu has learnt.
According to an analysis by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, the current contraction in domestic oil and gas production is due to factors that took place more than a decade ago.

However, since then, the government has taken steps such as increasing drilling and exploration to record levels, changing laws and rules to provide stable terms to explorers, and opening new avenues for exploration.

“The steps taken in the last few years — new acreage, record drilling, deepwater wells and the revival of Mumbai High — will start showing up in production over the next three to four years,” the note asserted. “That is the nature of this sector: the decisions of one decade decide the output of the next.”
The note also argues that now, unlike earlier, the profits of oil and gas companies upstream companies like ONGC and Oil India are being used to fund exploration rather than subsidies.
“Until 2015, ONGC and Oil India were made to fund a large share of the subsidy on diesel, LPG and kerosene, through discounts on the crude they sold to oil marketing companies,” the note said.

According to data with the Ministry, ONGC paid ₹49,421 crore towards this subsidy in 2012-13 against a profit of ₹20,926 crore, and in 2013-14 paid ₹56,384 crore towards this subsidy against a net profit of ₹22,095 crore.

“In both years ONGC gave away more than twice what it earned,” the note said. “Money that should have gone into finding new oil and gas went into keeping retail prices down. This burden was ended from 2015-16. ONGC now keeps its earnings and has sharply raised its spending on exploration.”
According to the latest data on the Index of Core Industries, the oil and gas sectors have contracted continuously for 22 and 28 months, respectively.

“In this sector it takes five to ten years to go from awarding a block to first production,” a note prepared by the Ministry and accessed by The Hindu said. “Output in 2026 is the result of what was, and was not, done a decade ago.

“After the ninth New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP) round was launched in 2010, no new exploration round was offered until 2016,” it added. “The fields producing today were not replaced by new ones in that period, and the effect is still being felt.”

The Ministry also stated that mature oil and gas fields generally lose 7-8% of their output every year as reservoir pressure falls and that most of India’s current production comes from such fields. On the other hand, new wells, enhanced recovery, and field redevelopment are making up much of the loss.

articles.title: SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has retained State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank in its 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), maintaining their respective positions under the same bucketing structure as in 2025.

Under the RBI’s framework, SBI, placed in Bucket 4, will have to maintain an additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital requirement of 0.80% of its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs). HDFC Bank, classified under Bucket 2, will have an additional CET1 requirement of 0.40%, while ICICI Bank, placed in Bucket 1, will have to maintain 0.20%.
These additional capital requirements are over and above the Capital Conservation Buffer, strengthening the banks’ ability to absorb financial shocks and contain systemic risks.

The latest classification is based on data collected from banks as of March 31, 2026. Under the D-SIB framework, banks are categorised into different buckets according to their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs), with higher scores attracting higher additional capital requirements.

The RBI introduced the Framework for Dealing with D-SIBs on July 22, 2014, subsequently updating it on December 28, 2023. The framework requires the central bank to publicly disclose the names of designated D-SIBs annually, beginning in 2015, and assign them to appropriate buckets based on their systemic importance.

SBI and ICICI Bank were initially designated as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016, respectively. HDFC Bank joined the list in 2017, when all three banks were identified as systemically important financial institutions.

articles.title: Core accountability: On core sector performance
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.

articles.title: Why are landmine casualties rising as the global ban comes under threat? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The story so far: Landmines and explosive remnants of war (ERW, meaning unexploded or abandoned ordnance) killed or injured more people in 2025 than in any year since 2020, according to the 28th annual Landmine Monitor report, which was released on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) by the International Campaign to Ban Landmines (ICBL). Its findings come as the Mine Ban Treaty, which bans antipersonnel mines, has seen its first-ever withdrawals.

The treaty came into force on March 1, 1999, after a campaign that won the ICBL the Nobel Peace Prize in 1997. Countries that join must stop the use, stockpiling, production, and transfer of antipersonnel mines. They must destroy their stockpiles within four years and clear mines in areas they control within 10 years. A total of 162 countries are now bound by the treaty, while 35 remain outside it.

Its findings come as the Mine Ban Treaty, which bans antipersonnel mines, has seen its first-ever withdrawals.
• The treaty came into force on March 1, 1999, after a campaign that won the ICBL the Nobel Peace Prize in 1997. fullParagraphs: A joint military training exercise between Nepal and India, focusing on disaster management, forest welfare and humanitarian assistance, commenced on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).
The 20th edition of the training exercise, “Abhyas Suryakiran”, began at Nepal Army Battle School in Saljhandi, Rupandehi district, according to a press release issued by the Nepal Army.
The exercise, involving battalion-level soldiers from the two countries, will run till December 8.

During the exercise, the military personnel of the two countries will exchange theoretical and practical aspects as well as special experiences relating to disaster management, forest warfare and humanitarian assistance, according to the Nepal Army.
The 19th edition of the joint military exercise was held in Uttarakhand’s Pithoragarh last year.

The Nepal Army believes such types of military exercises will further deepen friendly military relations between the two countries and also enhance professional skills and understanding between the soldiers of the two countries, the press release said.

articles.title: China launches crewed spaceship carrying first Pakistani astronaut to its space station
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: China on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) launched its Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship carrying three astronauts , including Pakistan’s Muhammad Zeeshan Ali , the first foreign national to participate in the country’s crewed space programme.
The spaceship, atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket, blasted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China, with officials declaring the launch successful minutes later.
The crew comprises mission commander and spacecraft pilot Tang Hongbo, flight engineer Wu Yi and Ali, who will become the first foreign astronaut to visit China’s orbiting Tiangong space station.
Mr. Ali will return to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft after spending about a week in orbit, while Chinese astronauts typically stay at the station for about six months.
The spacecraft is expected to dock with the Tiangong space station in a few hours.

China built its own space station after it was reportedly excluded from the International Space Station (ISS) over concerns about the involvement of its military, the People’s Liberation Army (PLA), in its space programme.
China is currently the only country operating its own space station, which became operational in 2022.
Tiangong is relatively small compared to the football pitch-sized ISS, where astronauts from several countries have conducted more than 3,000 experiments since its launch in 1998.
NASA plans to retire the ISS in early 2031, using a dedicated deorbit vehicle being developed by SpaceX to guide it into a controlled re-entry over the South Pacific, according to reports.

The Shenzhou-24 mission’s main objectives include completing an in-orbit crew rotation with the Shenzhou-23 crew, maintaining routine station operations, conducting scientific research and carrying out maintenance, public outreach and payload tests, Chinese officials said.
The flight stems from an agreement the two countries signed in February 2025. More than 90 scientific experiments and technology tests are planned during the mission.
These will cover space life sciences, materials science, microgravity fluid physics, combustion science, fundamental physics, space medicine and new space technologies, the officials said.

fullParagraphs: Two Indians were among those injured in an attack on a financial district in Riyadh that triggered strong condemnation from New Delhi.
India also denounced continued strikes targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

“Two Indians are among those injured in the attack on Riyadh financial district. The embassy of India in Riyadh is providing all possible assistance to the injured and their families,” the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said.
The attack was carried out on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). Local authorities said the injured included two Saudi citizens, three Nepalese and four Egyptian nationals.

The MEA said India strongly condemns the attack in Riyadh as well as the continued strikes targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. “These attacks seriously endanger civilian lives, violate the sovereignty of Saudi Arabia, and undermine regional security and stability. We call for immediate cessation of such attacks,” it said in a statement.

India also reiterated its firm solidarity with the people and government of Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed its unwavering support to the Kingdom in safeguarding its sovereignty and territorial integrity.
“We earnestly hope that peace and normalcy will return to the region at the earliest,” the MEA said.
There has been a sudden escalation in tensions in West Asia, especially after the Houthis carried out several strikes on Saudi Arabia.
The West Asia conflict began in February following attacks on Iran by the U.S. and Israel. New Delhi has consistently called for finding a solution to the conflict through dialogue and diplomacy.

India has been specifically voicing serious concern over the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia’s civilian infrastructure and economic assets, cautioning that such strikes undermine regional stability and threaten freedom of navigation through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.

articles.title: All you need to know about: Primary ciliary dyskinesia

fullParagraphs: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a rare inherited disorder that affects tiny, hair-like structures in the body called cilia. When these structures fail to move properly, mucus and bacteria accumulate in the airways, increasing the risk of recurrent respiratory infections and long-term lung damage.

While there is currently no cure, early diagnosis and regular treatment can help manage symptoms and preserve lung function. Recent research into the genetic causes of PCD is also offering new insights into the disease and its diagnosis.

articles.title: What is Beaver Supermoon, when is the next supermoon and more
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Skywatchers were treated to a dazzling view as the Beaver Supermoon lit up the night skies on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). The November full moon, known as the Beaver Moon, appears larger and brighter than usual due to its proximity to Earth. Here is more about the celestial display and when you can watch the next supermoon

The moon revolves around the Earth in an oval-shaped path (elliptical orbit). A supermoon occurs when the moon rises near perigee (the point in its orbit closest to earth), appearing larger and brighter than usual. This year’s full moon (November 24) is known as the Beaver Supermoon because this is when beavers prepare for the winter and also the time of year to set beaver traps before the swamps and rivers froze.

Supermoon appears 14 per cent bigger and 30 per cent brighter than a micromoon, which occurs when a full moon coincides with the moon being near its apogee — the farthest point from Earth in its orbit.
The “Beaver moon” is a moniker for November’s full moon adopted by the Old Farmer’s Almanac , supposedly from Algonquian languages once spoken by Native Americans in the New England territory.

Though not a rare occurrence, supermoons only happen three to four times a year and always appear consecutively. Because the Moon is in its closest point to Earth, it can cause higher tides than usual, according to NASA.
Supermoon is visible to the naked eye wherever skies are clear and no special equipment is required.
The next supermoon will be on December 24, 2026. The last supermoon of the year, it will be the largest full moon.
The first supermoon of 2027 will be on January 22, also known as the Wolf Supermoon.

‘Wolf moon’ is a traditional name for the first full moon that happens in January. Many full moons have old seasonal names, often popularised in folklore, that helped people keep track of the time of the year before the advent of modern calendars.

articles.title: When public duty meets medical privacy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Sonia Gandhi, in her recently published memoir, recalls being advised surgery for suspected breast cancer in 2010. Since she is a prominent public figure, she wonders, in her book, whether she was entitled to even a modicum of privacy with regard to her health. Her account assumes renewed significance following a recent petition before the Madras High Court that inquired about the health of Kolathur MLA V.S. Babu (now deceased). These episodes expose a fundamental legal tension between the privacy politicians may want about their health, and the accountability they owe their constituents in a democracy. Does the public’s right to information justify waiving or limiting an office-holder’s medical confidentiality? How should a democracy reconcile these competing interests?

Medical information is among the most sensitive forms of personal information. A diagnosis may reveal not merely someone’s present condition but also their reproductive history, genetic predispositions, psychiatric illness or future health risks. Disclosure can invite discrimination, political exploitation and public speculation. In Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017), the Supreme Court recognised privacy as a fundamental right under Article 21. Holding public office does not automatically extinguish this protection. A politician receiving treatment need not publish laboratory reports. Nor does a disability establish an inability to govern. State intrusion needs lawful justification, not curiosity.

The Constitution does not prescribe a general medical-fitness requirement for occupying high public office. Article 58 sets eligibility conditions for the President but requires no medical-fitness certificate. Article 65(2) allows the Vice-President to perform presidential functions when the President cannot do so through absence, illness or another cause. The Constitution recognises presidential illness but does not specify a detailed procedure or medical authority to determine contested incapacity. This distinction between eligibility to assume office and capacity to continue functioning deserves closer scrutiny.

For legislators, Articles 102 and 191 prescribe disqualification when a person is of ‘unsound mind’ and stands so declared by a competent court (not by a medical board). Section 16(1)(b) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, similarly provides for disqualification from electoral registration (by court not medical board). For Supreme Court judges, Article 124(4) permits removal on proof of incapacity, while the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968, provides a procedure that may involve a Medical Board. Article 317(3)(c), governing Public Service Commission members, permits removal for unfitness arising from ‘infirmity of mind or body’.

articles.title: The cow, the flea and the genome: One Health and the statecraft of prevention
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: In the second of his Major Rock Edicts, cut into stone in the third century BCE, Ashoka records that he has provided medical care of two kinds, for people and for animals, and has had healing herbs planted wherever they were lacking. Twenty-three centuries before the phrase existed, an Indian State treated the health of humans, animals and the land as a single charge of government. Rudolf Virchow, who introduced the word ‘zoonosis’, restated the idea for the age of the microscope: between animal and human medicine there is no dividing line, nor should there be.

Modern governance, however, forgot what Ashoka and Virchow knew. It allotted people to one ministry, livestock to another and forests to a third, and pathogens, which recognise no such allocation of business, have exploited the gaps ever since. One Health, which the world marks on November 3, is the effort to recover that lost unity with the tools of the 21st century by bringing human, animal and environmental health into a common framework for research, surveillance and prevention. The Indian philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam , which regards the world as one family, resonates with this understanding of interconnected life.

This year the case makes itself. Lumpy skin disease (LSD) has returned to India. The September forecast from ICAR-National Institute of Veterinary Epidemiology and Disease Informatics’ early-warning system placed 219 districts across 28 states and Union Territories at risk, and Rajasthan had recorded more than 10,400 cases in 10 eastern districts by mid-September. In Siberia, a young technician at Irkutsk’s anti-plague institute died in early October, of what Russian authorities called pneumonia of unknown cause, amid reports of pneumonic plague. Nearly 200 people were placed under observation. Whatever the final diagnosis, Yersinia pestis , the organism of the Black Death, has never left us. It persists in rodents and their fleas, from the marmots of the Central Asian steppe to the prairie dogs of New Mexico and the rats of Madagascar.

Neither story respects a departmental boundary. LSD does not infect people, but it drains milk cans, household incomes and children’s nutrition. Plague is at once a problem of wildlife ecology, laboratory biosafety, clinical medicine and public trust.

articles.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang says he is in therapy as comeback rally fades
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Jensen Huang apologised to Nvidia staff and said he was in therapy on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as a stock rally triggered by his shock return as CEO faltered amid persistent doubts over the probes he faces and the fate of the AI investment boom.

"I made some terrible mistakes," Mr. Huang told an hourlong all-hands meeting at the company's Santa Clara, California, headquarters, The New York Times reported after reviewing a livestream of the event.
He told staff it was "not acceptable" that he had broken a code of conduct he had helped write, and dismissed suggestions that he was back because U.S. President Donald Trump had pressured the board.
But Mr. Trump told CNBC on Monday (November 23, 2026) that he had been in contact with directors about Mr. Huang's return. "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," he said. "And I convinced them."
After vaulting more than 30% on Monday (November 23, 2026), Nvidia shares were down about six percent at close on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).
"The optimism faded quickly" for Nvidia, wrote Fawad Razaqzada of Forex.com, with "questions over corporate governance and board oversight still lingering."
So far Monday's surge was a "one day wonder...We are not seeing an upside follow through today at all," said Ken Mahoney, president and CEO of Mahoney Asset Management.

Mr. Huang resigned on November 12 over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, a departure that sent shares in Nvidia and companies closely linked to the AI buildout tumbling.
Mr. Trump was reportedly talked into backing the return of the Taiwan-born CEO after top tech investors told him the U.S. economy and Wall Street depended on it.
Nvidia said Monday (November 23, 2026) that it had reinstated Mr. Huang as chief executive after receiving information from the US government that he did not pose a national security risk.
Mr. Trump is also an investor in Nvidia, owning as many as 370,000 shares in the company as of September 30, according to filings.
Shares linked to the AI boom have fallen steeply in recent weeks amid fears that the AI bubble, inflated since the launch of ChatGPT in 2022, was finally bursting.

articles.title: Workers in high-risk jobs to receive shots against rabies in Tamil Nadu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Over a lakh persons belonging to high-risk occupational groups, including animal handlers and dog catchers of local bodies, in all 38 districts will receive Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) against rabies under the Tamil Nadu State Action Plan for Dog-Mediated Rabies Elimination (SAPRE) - Vision 2030.

The State government has given the administrative sanction for implementation of the initiative at a cost of ₹2.22 crore, which will be met from the National Health Mission, Tamil Nadu, an order issued recently said.
In just four months of 2026, Tamil Nadu records 2.63 lakh dog bites, 17 deaths
Gaps in anti-rabies treatment persist in Chennai’s health centres

The Directorate of Public Health (DPH) and Preventive Medicine noted that certain occupational groups are routinely exposed to dogs and other animals in the course of their duties. Provision of PrEP to such identified high-risk personnel will provide an additional layer of protection and strengthen the State’s rabies elimination strategy.
The programme aims to provide PrEP to identified personnel of occupational groups having sustained risk of exposure to dogs and other potentially rabid animals.

The main categories include sanitation workers, animal handlers and dog catchers of local bodies and eligible personnel of the Animal Husbandry Department involved in animal handling, dog catching, veterinary and para-veterinary activities.

As per the National Guidelines on Rabies Prophylaxis, eligibility will be determined based on occupational exposure risk and the nature of duties performed. Based on the presently available department data, the preliminary beneficiary estimation was 1,29,009 - 1,21,844 local body sanitation workers, 3,324 local body animal handlers/dog catchers and 3,841 personnel attached to the Animal Husbandry department, the directorate said.

The initiative will be implemented through designated government health facilities, including Primary Health Centres (PHC), Urban PHCs, government hospitals, and medical college hospitals. Identification of beneficiaries and mobilisation will be carried out by the respective local bodies and Animal Husbandry Department.

articles.title: Beyond generosity: on India-Nepal ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The state visit of Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah to Delhi, eight months after he was voted to power as leader of the ‘GenZ’ movement that ousted the previous government, was anticipated as a chance to reset the turbulent India-Nepal relationship. Bringing Mr. Shah to India for a state visit, his first, was particularly important, given the Modi government’s tense ties with his predecessor K.P. Sharma Oli’s government; Mr. Oli was not invited to Delhi more than a year into his term and travelled to Beijing instead. Initially, Mr. Shah had also given New Delhi some worrying moments, with comments about boundary disputes, and a refusal to confirm a meeting with Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri, which led to the cancellation of his visit in May. Subsequently, some of the realities of governance, particularly after the massive flash flood in August , have warmed Delhi-Kathmandu relations. Following talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Mr. Shah thanked India for its immediate and unstinting support in the flood relief and rescue operations. Mr. Modi’s praise for Mr. Shah indicated the forging of a personal rapport on which to build the road map for ties. India announced a Development Cooperation Package — a generous ₹15,000 crore (about $1.6 billion) — for reconstruction and long-term development in Nepal. Another announcement, to offer Nepal access to Indian ports in Gujarat and Odisha, will go a long way in helping land-locked Nepal, particularly given the bilateral bad blood over the 2015 trade blockade. The inauguration of bridges, roads, trains, energy and fuel lines, an Integrated Check post (ICP) and an agreement to set up an IIT (its third offshore campus) are all signs of concrete plans to improve relations, as outlined in the joint statement titled “Viksit Bharat and Samunnat Nepal: Re-imagining the Partnership”.

Despite some of the heated rhetoric over ties, both sides appeared to have decided to deal with areas of differences in a less public manner. Mr. Shah’s persistent comments on the boundary dispute, and long-pending request for overflight access for two debt-ridden airports, were not dealt with directly, but in a broad reference about resolving “all outstanding matters” through dialogue. While the joint statement also said they would review all bilateral treaties, New Delhi’s contention that the “Eminent Persons Group” (EPG) report that suggested important changes to the 1950 Friendship treaty, is now “not relevant”, will ruffle feathers in Kathmandu which has been keen to update the treaty. The government must remember that along with the grand gestures, it is important to keep a close eye on Nepal’s grievances as well. If disregarded, these can trip up the broader progress and conception of the bilateral relationship, as spelt out by both leaders.

articles.title: Spinning wheels: on urban mobility in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: While Karnataka has spent years disputing motorcycle owners’ right to carry paying passengers, Bengaluru — with the dubious distinction of having one of the world’s highest travel times per unit distance — struggles with inadequate public transport capacity and lacklustre intermediate options. The Supreme Court ruling on November 20 to dismiss Karnataka’s appeal was thus straightforward, allowing motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles. The State has often called bike taxis unsafe, yet has not improved the prospects of safer options. Earlier this year, the Centre for Science and Environment estimated the number of buses in urban centres nationwide to be 70% short of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs benchmark and that 400 cities with populations between a lakh and 10 lakh altogether lacked organised bus services. In March, the BMTC reported a fleet of around 7,000 buses in Bengaluru, versus the 13,000 by 2025 envisaged by the Comprehensive Mobility Plan. Expanding the number of Metro stations also creates more demand for travel to and from stations, but the operating costs of the public transport corporation expected to serve that demand are not covered by the resulting increase in rail ridership.

Overall, Karnataka has struggled to set up a consistent transport policy. An expert committee recommended against bike taxis in Bengaluru for first- and last-mile connectivity and in favour of better walking infrastructure and bicycle rentals in 2019, only for the State to launch the electric bike-taxi scheme in 2021, then rescind it in 2024 over safety concerns and drivers’ disputes. The market for short booked journeys is also dysfunctional. But while allowing bike taxis could temper autorickshaw fares, the State must investigate drivers’ operating costs, the difference between the paid and the received amounts, and prevent large platforms from exploiting the market. Finally, while the Union Road Transport Ministry has reported that 46.2% of all road deaths involved two-wheeler users, two-wheelers’ safety relative to autorickshaws and cabs, by the number and distance of journeys, is unclear. The State should require aggregators to report injuries and fatalities and investigate the consequences of drivers’ earnings being linked to the number of trips undertaken. The Union government’s 2025 Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines already address passenger security, fares, and insurance while allowing States to authorise privately registered motorcycles through aggregators. Karnataka should exercise this additional power. A large national programme is required to address funding for public transport, which is necessary even when it is not immediately profitable.

articles.title: Fatal disagreement: on the COP31 summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: COP31 ended in Antalya, Türkiye, with a whimper. The 190-odd countries that had convened for nearly 12 days — a close to 50-hour overshoot — failed to agree on an overarching political statement , called a cover text, that acts as a stepping stone to future, collective global action on climate change. Usually, cover texts evolve as a final synthesis of deliberations ; the COP31 leadership, helmed by Türkiye and Australia, thought it fit to push for a cover text early in the proceedings. The headline sought was a global electrification target: 35% of global final energy consumption will come from electricity by 2035, in the hope that this would reduce direct fossil fuel emissions. Ultimately, the cover text failed to pass muster because the European Union objected to the text’s lack of any explicit mention of ‘fossil fuel,’ let alone its phase-out. The COP process is arduously protracted as even a single country’s objection can stall progress. Country-blocks outside the EU, such as coalitions of the least developed countries, island nations, some South American countries — reportedly 130 countries — were also insistent on fossil fuel language. While COP 31 made some progress on old pathways, such as the Just Transition agreement, it is perplexing that the delegations could not make progress on the other big prong of negotiations: climate finance.

The increase in solar panel installations and the significant shift towards battery use in grid storage and transport did not come cheap: the cost of the land required for their installation, their intermittent nature of being dependent on weather, grid upgrades all carry costs. It is global markets, imperfectly connected, but connected, that have managed to bring it to this stage over decades. India and China, major fossil emitters, with large, still indigent populations, are also leaders in total clean energy installations. Therefore it stands to reason that developed countries, which have committed to providing climate finance in recognition of their historical emissions, make good on past promises to shoulder the cost of the carbon emissions that are responsible for warming. Economic crises are a feature, and not a bug, of the interconnected financial system enveloping the world and there are, undeniably, challenges to diverting the necessary finance towards countries most vulnerable to climate change impact. However, it is no longer prudent to sweep this under the rug by scuttling experimental approaches — namely carbon capture — as inimical to the broader commitment to eschew fossil fuel. When the primary framework climate agreement was crafted three decades ago, nobody envisaged AI and the drain that data centres portended or the wars that would see the vociferous antagonists of coal immediately shore up their gas reserves. Without honest good-faith dialogue, the COP is at risk of being a sideshow: a mortal blow to multilateralism.

articles.title: Just verdict: on Myanmar and the International Court of Justice
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: On November 19, the International Court of Justice held that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. It is for the first time that the court has found any state responsible for the crime. The verdict, with nine votes to six, was not lightly reached. Genocide requires proof of an intent to destroy a group. In the absence of direct evidence of a plan, the court could infer that intent only if it was “the only reasonable inference” from the facts, a high bar to affix responsibility. The facts it accepted are harrowing. In 2017, in what Myanmar’s army called “clearance operations” against the insurgent Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed, 1,834 raped and 392 villages destroyed in northern Rakhine State. Over 7,00,000 fled to Bangladesh. Then Army chief Min Aung Hlaing, now Myanmar’s “civilian” President, called the “Bengali problem” an “unfinished job”. Myanmar argued that it had only been fighting insurgents or at worst, driving the Rohingya out or punishing them. The court said that the army drew no distinction between fighters and civilians, had no plan to move anyone, fired on fleeing people and killed children on a scale that could not be explained as punishment. Seen alongside decades of discrimination, the evidence pointed to an intent to destroy.

The incidents of 2017 were no aberration. The army drove lakhs of Rohingya into Bangladesh in 1978 and 1991-92. The junta stripped the Rohingya of citizenship in 1982 and the state branded them as “foreigners” in Arakan, disenfranchising them in 2015. While the junta’s Bamar-Buddhist vision has oppressed every minority, the Rohingya have been subjected to the most brutality. More than 1.2 million are in Bangladesh, living in dilapidated conditions, made worse due to diminished international aid. The court ordered Myanmar to allow their safe, voluntary and dignified return and to compensate them, but it has no means of enforcing its judgment. Only the UN Security Council can, but it will be subject to vetoes by Myanmar’s backers, China and Russia. articles.title: Core accountability: On core sector performance
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.

articles.title: Paper tiger: On the Green India Mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: That all was not well with the Green India Mission was clear even before its approval. After the UPA-I government announced it in 2008, the Ministry of Rural Development had objected to its financial design much before the Union Cabinet approved it in 2014. But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The outlay was ₹46,000 crore. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. In 2021-22, the Ministry folded the NAP into the Mission and, in mid-2025, unveiled a revised version with an allocation of ₹12,190 crore to improve forest cover on 25 mha by 2030, including 24 mha through other schemes. The government had thus expanded the primary target but left the Mission responsible for only 1 mha.

Together with the CAMPA, NAP, and MGNREGS funds never materialising, it is no surprise that the programmes to improve forest quality and forest cover have respectively fallen short by 91.8% and 97.5% vis-à-vis the 2014 target. The Environment Ministry had assembled a large programme around resources that it knew it could not control. Pro-climate work in practice ought to span government schemes to deliver action and justice, and the Ministry ought to have formalised the division of responsibilities and accounting system. The PAC’s new demand that the Ministry submit an implementation timetable is insufficient. From the Jal Shakti Abhiyan in 2019 to the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan in 2024, the government has often floated new programmes banking significantly on funds from existing schemes — an untenable policy when the latter also have their own obligations. And if the VB-G RAM G scheme was to also advance climate justice, the government should not have undermined the erstwhile demand-driven funding model and shifted more financial responsibility to the States. Climate action has to be timely, for which the Union government must dedicate adequate resources and proactively ensure that its initiatives are implemented.

articles.title: Gold, silver price fall boosts retail sales but raises concerns among jewellers in Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The sharp decline in gold and silver prices over the past 15 days has brought relief to jewellery buyers, particularly those planning weddings and purchasing precious metals for gifting, even as it has raised concerns among investors and traders over potential losses.
While jewellers have reported an increase in sales following the decline in prices, industry representatives remain divided over its impact on businesses and the future movement of prices.

According to market rates on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), 24-carat gold was priced at ₹12,780 per gram, down from around ₹18,000 per gram in January 2026. Prices had remained in the range of ₹15,000 to ₹16,000 per gram during September and October. Silver prices have also witnessed a steep decline, falling from around ₹3.5 lakh and ₹4 lakh per kg to ₹1.6 lakh per kg.

Srinivas R., honorary secretary of the Jewellers Association, Bengaluru, said that the gold prices had declined by around 34%, while silver prices had fallen by nearly 60%, creating both opportunities and challenges for different sections of the market.

“The current situation can be analysed in two ways. It is a good time for those who want to purchase gold and silver for weddings or gift them to their loved ones. However, it is definitely not a good time for investors who purchased precious metals earlier, expecting good returns or profits from selling them. They may have to wait for the next two months. As per my prediction, gold prices could decline further to around ₹11,500 per gram,” he said.

T.A. Sharavana, founder and owner of Shree Sai Gold Palace, said that jewellery shops have witnessed an increase in sales over the past 15 days as customers sought to take advantage of the lower prices.

“This is the first time in history that gold prices have risen to ₹18,000 per gram and subsequently fallen to around ₹12,000 within just 10 months. A similar trend has been witnessed in silver prices,” he said.

However, he pointed out that the price correction could adversely affect newly established jewellery businesses, particularly those that had borrowed money from banks and private financiers to set up their shops and purchase inventory.

“Established businesses that have been operating for several years may be able to absorb or compensate for the losses. However, newly opened shops could face difficulties. According to my calculation, gold and silver businesses could incur losses of around 25%, considering the expenditure on employee salaries, electricity bills and other operational costs,” he added.

Disagreeing with the assessment of losses, B. Ramachary, president of the Karnataka State Jewellers Federation (KSJW), said the decline in prices would not necessarily translate into losses for most jewellery businesses.

He said several jewellers would have purchased gold and silver at lower prices in January and February and sold them to customers when rates were significantly higher, ranging between ₹15,000 and ₹18,000 per gram. The profits earned during that period, he said, could offset any losses arising from the current price correction.
Mr. Ramachary also advised those planning to invest in gold and silver to wait until December 9, when the U.S. Federal Reserve is scheduled to review its interest rates.

articles.title: Maharashtra panel recommends ₹10 crore fine, life imprisonment for those guilty of exam paper leaks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: People involved in leaking recruitment examination papers should be punished with a fine of ₹10 crore and life imprisonment, according to the recommendations of a committee set up by the Maharashtra government, which submitted its report on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

The panel, headed by the director of the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, also proposed a framework to oversee the process of conducting tests, including a third party audit and a new body to manage exam venues.

This committee was set up in the wake of a paper leak in an examination to recruit pharmacists and drug inspectors for 954 posts, conducted by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission on March 22. It was later discovered that the paper had already been leaked on WhatsApp, leading to the cancellation of the recruitment process on August 25, and an investigation into the matter. The State government set up the committee on September 4, after candidates sought a review of the exam process to recommend changes in the system.

Apart from a recommended penalty of a ₹10 crore fine and life imprisonment for individuals involved in paper leaks, the panel called for the establishment of a task force to address leak incidents, courts for the disposal of cases, and a body to manage exam venues, to bring accountability to district officials and prevent such leaks.

The panel proposes a third party audit, a cyber security cell, surveillance cameras, and signal-blocking devices at venues. Police personnel should be appointed to the Commission’s teams and non-governmental institutions need to be monitored to reduce irregularities in the selection of venues, the committee said. It also called for the publication of statistics regarding vacant posts and the development of a portal to resolve issues faced by candidates.

With regard to the pharmacist selection exam, the report recommends a fee refund by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission for all candidates who file income tax returns. The panel also suggested an increase in the number of posts for the Group-C exam, an extra attempt for candidates, an exam schedule to be announced by October, and a grievance portal to ensure transparency.

articles.title: KSEB revokes suspension of engineer over power disruption during Minister’s programme in Kannur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) has revoked the suspension of Satheesh Babu P.V., a sub-engineer attached to the Kannur electrical section. He was suspended following a power disruption during a programme attended by Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph at the Jawahar Library Hall in Kannur on November 21.

The suspension was withdrawn through an order issued by the executive engineer on Tuesday (November 24), following a review of the circumstances surrounding the incident and the report submitted by senior officials. Mr. Babu had been suspended pending inquiry after power supply was disrupted during the Minister’s programme on the morning of November 21.
The decision to reconsider the suspension followed a direction from the Deputy Chief Engineer, Electrical Circle, Kannur, on November 23.
In his report, the assistant executive engineer said that the official was unaware of the programme attended by the Minister and had intended to carry out routine maintenance work.
The suspension had triggered protests from KSEB employees’ organisations.

articles.title: Demand gets louder for restrictions on nightlife at Kozhikode beach
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nightlife at the Kozhikode beach and surrounding areas, one of the major tourist attractions in the city, is in the news, with residents seeking restrictions on people’s activities there in view of the reported involvement of anti-social elements.

District Collector M.S. Madhavikutty and District Police Chief (Kozhikode City) A.P. Shoukathali conducted a surprise inspection of the stretch from the South Beach to Konnad Beach on November 21. They were accompanied by officials from the departments of Port, Fisheries, and Health, and those from the district tourism promotion council and the Kozhikode Corporation. In view of a special branch report citing safety concerns, the officials examined complaints related to a lack of proper lighting in the area, broken tiles, disposal of waste, and the management of wastewater from the Food Street on the beach.

The special branch had reportedly said that restrictions could be imposed in places that lacked proper lighting and security arrangements. Though the stretch from the open stage to Mukhadar beach is relatively secure, areas such as Butt Road, Kothi beach, and Konnad beach are in a pitiable condition. Otherwise, if the YSRCP comes to power in the 2029 Assembly elections, it will take stern action against the officials,” said Mr. Prasada.

articles.title: Guru Nanak’s message of equality, harmony resonates at Prakash Purab
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Thousands of Sikh devotees and people from other faiths gathered at Nampally Exhibition Grounds on Tuesday to celebrate the 557th Prakash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism, with prayers, devotional music and a community meal.

The congregation, held on the occasion of Guru Nanak’s birth anniversary, was jointly organised by the managing committees of Gurudwara Sri Guru Singh Sabha, Ashok Bazar, and Gurudwara Saheb, Secunderabad. The programme began at 11 am and continued until 4.30 pm.
Devotees offered prayers before the Sri Guru Granth Sahib, the holy scripture of Sikhism, followed by Gurbani kirtan and katha (religious discourse).

Ragi jathas (groups of devotional singers) from different parts of the country performed shabads, including Bhai Maninder Singh of Sri Darbar Sahib, Amritsar, and Bhai Kamaldeep Singh and Bhai Jagteshwar Singh of Patiala. Their renditions highlighted spiritual values and the importance of communal harmony.

Addressing the congregation, preachers recalled Guru Nanak’s teachings of belief in one God, equality irrespective of caste, creed or gender, honest living and selfless service. They said his message continue to hold relevance in a world often divided by social and religious differences.

The celebrations concluded with Guru Ka Langar, the community kitchen tradition in which devotees, irrespective of faith or social background, sat together in rows and shared a meal, reflecting Guru Nanak’s principle of equality and service.

articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.
Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return.
Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling.

“Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation.
“Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.”
The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23).
The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025.
Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.
The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

Neocloud and data-center companies, which came under sharp selling pressure earlier following Mr. Huang’s abrupt exit, also climbed. CoreWeave rose 21.5%, IREN gained 26.4% and Nebius advanced ⁠23.4%.
The S&P 500 information technology sector jumped 8.9% and led the gains in the benchmark index.

articles.title: Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 years as recent measures take effect, Petroleum Ministry says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The government expects domestic oil and gas production to pick up in the next 4-5 years as several steps taken in the recent past begin to bear fruit in an industry typically characterised by long gestation periods, The Hindu has learnt.
According to an analysis by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, the current contraction in domestic oil and gas production is due to factors that took place more than a decade ago.

However, since then, the government has taken steps such as increasing drilling and exploration to record levels, changing laws and rules to provide stable terms to explorers, and opening new avenues for exploration.

“The steps taken in the last few years — new acreage, record drilling, deepwater wells and the revival of Mumbai High — will start showing up in production over the next three to four years,” the note asserted. “That is the nature of this sector: the decisions of one decade decide the output of the next.”
The note also argues that now, unlike earlier, the profits of oil and gas companies upstream companies like ONGC and Oil India are being used to fund exploration rather than subsidies.
“Until 2015, ONGC and Oil India were made to fund a large share of the subsidy on diesel, LPG and kerosene, through discounts on the crude they sold to oil marketing companies,” the note said.

According to data with the Ministry, ONGC paid ₹49,421 crore towards this subsidy in 2012-13 against a profit of ₹20,926 crore, and in 2013-14 paid ₹56,384 crore towards this subsidy against a net profit of ₹22,095 crore.

“In both years ONGC gave away more than twice what it earned,” the note said. “Money that should have gone into finding new oil and gas went into keeping retail prices down. This burden was ended from 2015-16. ONGC now keeps its earnings and has sharply raised its spending on exploration.”
According to the latest data on the Index of Core Industries, the oil and gas sectors have contracted continuously for 22 and 28 months, respectively.

“In this sector it takes five to ten years to go from awarding a block to first production,” a note prepared by the Ministry and accessed by The Hindu said. “Output in 2026 is the result of what was, and was not, done a decade ago.

“After the ninth New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP) round was launched in 2010, no new exploration round was offered until 2016,” it added. “The fields producing today were not replaced by new ones in that period, and the effect is still being felt.”

The Ministry also stated that mature oil and gas fields generally lose 7-8% of their output every year as reservoir pressure falls and that most of India’s current production comes from such fields. On the other hand, new wells, enhanced recovery, and field redevelopment are making up much of the loss.

articles.title: SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has retained State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank in its 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), maintaining their respective positions under the same bucketing structure as in 2025.

Under the RBI’s framework, SBI, placed in Bucket 4, will have to maintain an additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital requirement of 0.80% of its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs). HDFC Bank, classified under Bucket 2, will have an additional CET1 requirement of 0.40%, while ICICI Bank, placed in Bucket 1, will have to maintain 0.20%.
These additional capital requirements are over and above the Capital Conservation Buffer, strengthening the banks’ ability to absorb financial shocks and contain systemic risks.

The latest classification is based on data collected from banks as of March 31, 2026. Under the D-SIB framework, banks are categorised into different buckets according to their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs), with higher scores attracting higher additional capital requirements.

The RBI introduced the Framework for Dealing with D-SIBs on July 22, 2014, subsequently updating it on December 28, 2023. The framework requires the central bank to publicly disclose the names of designated D-SIBs annually, beginning in 2015, and assign them to appropriate buckets based on their systemic importance.

SBI and ICICI Bank were initially designated as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016, respectively. HDFC Bank joined the list in 2017, when all three banks were identified as systemically important financial institutions.

articles.title: Core accountability: On core sector performance
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: While welcoming Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for prioritising locally-made products and reducing gold imports, the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has said that India must balance “economic patriotism” and its cultural traditions when it comes to gold jewellery.

It argued that the sector contributes “nearly 7-8%” to the economy and supports “millions of livelihoods”. The GJC was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent and repeated appeal to all Indians to stop foreign trips and weddings, to buy local, and to only buy gold if necessary.

“The Prime Minister’s appeal for economic patriotism and greater preference for Swadeshi products is timely and welcome,” Rajesh Rokde, Chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said.

“While we fully support the Prime Minister’s call for restraint when gold is viewed purely as bullion or an investment instrument, jewellery consumption remains closely linked to culture, craftsmanship, and livelihoods,” Mr. Rokde added.
He said that gold and jewellery hold a unique place in India’s cultural heritage, particularly during festive and wedding seasons, such as the period that India will soon enter in October-December.
“The jewellery industry, contributing nearly 7-8% to the economy and supporting millions of livelihoods, is an integral part of India’s growth story,” Mr. Rokde asserted.
‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal

“As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and alignment with national priorities — balancing economic patriotism with India’s enduring cultural traditions,” he added.
